text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — we ran the prototype of the quota-delegation gateway last week. Proposal recap: an edge proxy issues short-lived "quota vouchers" to frontdoor proxies. Vouchers encode allowances (tokens, TTL, route scope) and are HMAC-signed by the central quota service. Advantages: lower central QPS, faster admission at the edge, and simpler local fairness decisions.

aj: Can you clarify how this affects global fairness? If edges make local decisions based on vouchers, won't we lose cross-tenant smoothing?

maria: Good point. The idea is vouchers are minted from central fair-scheduler outputs, i.e., central still computes per-tenant budgets periodically (every N seconds) and mints vouchers that reflect the current allocation. Edges consume vouchers deterministically. So global fairness is preserved at the cadence of voucher issuance; there will be short windows of local autonomy.

sam: How do we handle abuse / double-spend? If a voucher leaks, anyone could replay it at multiple edges. Also what about idempotency across retries?

maria: We considered replay. Plan: vouchers include a nonce and an optional origin binding (edge-id). Replay prevention is enforced by central when vouchers are redeemed (we expect most redemptions to be consumed locally without round-trip). To reduce central churn we use a two-tier design: small-value vouchers (micro-allowances) can be validated solely by signature and local counters; larger or suspicious redemptions require central reconciliation.

kai: Telemetry and debugging will be a pain. If an app hits a deny locally, we need to know if it's due to local exhaustion or central policy change. What traces / headers do we surface?

maria: Plan to add two headers for visibility: `X-Quota-Voucher` (base64 voucher) and `X-Quota-Source: edge|central`. Edges will emit structured logs on voucher consumption with fields: tenant, voucher_id, remaining_allowance, local_counter. We'll also attach `quota.trace_id` to spans for sampling.

aj: Nice. Operationally, what is the failure mode when central is unavailable? Do edges stop accepting requests?

maria: Edges operate in degraded mode: continue accepting requests using cached vouchers until TTL expiry. If central is down and vouchers expire, fallback policy is to switch to a conservative global cap (configured per env) to avoid blowouts. We avoid a hard deny across the fleet.

sam: About fairness scheduling: if central mints vouchers with coarse granularity (say 10s windows), does that make bursty clients get disproportionate share during their window? Could be gamed.

maria: True — we have two mitigations: 1) vary the window slightly (jitter) and 2) use shape-based allocations (not flat token counts) so the voucher includes a curve (e.g., tokens per-second) rather than a single lump. Edges enforce that curve.

kai: Implementation question: how big are vouchers and what's the crypto cost? We need to avoid per-request HMAC verification overhead for common paths.

maria: Vouchers are compact (JWT-like, ~200 bytes). For hot paths we plan to use hardware-accelerated HMAC and LRU cache for validated voucher IDs. Also allow edges to batch-verify by voucher prefix heuristics.

sam: Need to see header / sample voucher.

maria: Example voucher header (sketch):
```
X-Quota-Voucher: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ0ZW5hbnQiOiJhbWMiLCJpZCI6IjEyMyIsInRvdGFsIjoxMDAsInR0bCI6MTc4NTQzMjE2MCwibm9uY2UiOiJhYmMxMjMifQ.SIG

{"voucher_id":"abc123","tenant":"acme","allowance":100,"ttl":1785432160,"shape":"burst=10,rate=5/s"}
```

aj: Can we make voucher introspection cheap? It would help to have a small in-memory identity map for recent vouchers rather than re-parsing every request.

maria: Agreed — edges keep a small cache keyed by voucher_id with parsed policy and remaining allowance. Cache eviction is LRU and size is configurable.

kai: How does this interact with per-route vs per-tenant quotas? Some routes are metered differently (embeddings vs generate).

maria: Voucher scope includes route tags. Central mints route-aware vouchers. Edges reject mismatched route usage. That keeps accounting correct while still allowing central to shape allocation across classes.

sam: One more concern: billing alignment. We must ensure vouchers map to billing records so customers see correct usage. If edges consume vouchers locally, how do we export accurate usage?

maria: Edges periodically batch-emit redemption logs to central usage pipeline. Each entry is annotated with voucher_id, tenant, route, and tokens consumed. Central reconciles batched events and falls back to central reconciliation if batches are missing. We'll sign batches to prevent tampering.

deploy-bot: RFC doc created: https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/quota-delegation-gateway — please add implementation risks to the draft.

aj: Action items: (1) add replay protection design and abuse detection hooks, (2) define TTL/window jitter defaults, (3) sketch rollout plan (canary edges + monitoring). I'll take (3).

maria: Thanks — I'll update RFC with the nonce/HMAC sketch and telemetry fields. Sam, Kai — can you review the replay/telemetry sections by EOD? :thumbsup:
